newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst shares fall on AgrEvo sales plan.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst shares fall on AgrEvo sales plan.

text.p: Shares in German chemicals group Hoechst AG fell in bourse trade on Friday after analysts were sceptical the group's AgrEvo unit would achieve its forecast sales targets.
Shares in Hoechst fell 46 pfennigs to 53.48 marks, a drop of nearly 0.9 percent, running counter to the overall market which was up 0.83 percent at 2,591.73 points.
Analysts said they doubted the group could meet its sales targets.
Late on Thursday in New York AgrEvo, the crop protection unit Hoechst runs jointly with Germany's Schering AG, said it will post sales of $3.6 billion this year.
Hoechst owns 60 percent of Agrevo, while Schering holds the remaining 40 percent.
